name: Disorder of Vitamin and Non-Protein Cofactor Absorption and Transport

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Vitamin and Cofactor Absorption Disorders

criteria.description: Presence of clinical symptoms consistent with vitamin or cofactor deficiency despite adequate dietary intake
Biochemical evidence of low serum vitamin or cofactor levels with normal dietary intake
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in vitamin or cofactor absorption or transport
Exclusion of other causes of malabsorption or nutritional deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical presentation, laboratory evidence, and genetic testing) must be met for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may require multidisciplinary evaluation including nutritional, genetic, and gastroenterological assessments.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes peripheral neuropathy and developmental delay
searchTerms: severe vitamin deficiency with nerve symptoms
low vitamin levels causing neurological problems

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked failure to thrive despite adequate nutrition
searchTerms: failure to thrive with normal diet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent metabolic acidosis due to cofactor deficiency
searchTerms: ongoing acid buildup due to missing cofactors

common.symptomName: Macrocytic anemia secondary to vitamin B12 deficiency
searchTerms: large red blood cell anemia from B12 lack
macrocytic anemia caused by vitamin B12 deficiency
anemia with big red blood cells
chronic loose stools from poor nutrient absorption
eye problems including optic nerve damage
repeated infections due to weak immunity
heart muscle disease from cofactor deficiency
heart problems due to nutrient shortage

occasional.symptomName: Psychiatric symptoms including irritability and cognitive impairment
searchTerms: mood changes with irritability and memory issues
psychiatric symptoms like irritability and cognitive decline

laboratory: Low serum levels of specific vitamins (e.g., B12, folate, biotin)
Elevated methylmalonic acid and homocysteine levels
Macrocytic anemia on complete blood count
imaging: MRI showing cerebral atrophy or demyelination in severe cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes encoding vitamin transporters (e.g., SLC19A2, TCN2)
other: Abnormal vitamin absorption tests (e.g., Schilling test)

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated vitamin B12 deficiency without multi-vitamin malabsorption
Specific mutations in intrinsic factor or cubilin genes
Pancreatic insufficiency causing fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption
Characteristic pulmonary and sweat chloride abnormalities

redFlags: Rapid neurological deterioration with progressive neuropathy
Severe metabolic acidosis refractory to standard treatment
Failure to thrive despite adequate nutritional support
